subject: SDG Weekly Compass - Week of 2026-10-26
overview_zh: 本周看点是电动化、AI与工业减排都已进入制度设计阶段。

items.title_en: Chart: A record two-thirds of car sales in China are now electric vehicles
items.summary_zh: Carbon Brief 通过中国乘联会数据指出，2026年9月新能源车占新车销量67%，在油价上升和燃油车需求下滑的背景下，电动化已从政策扶持转向市场自我强化，并开始通过出口扩张影响全球汽车产业与石油需求。
items.core_argument_zh: Carbon Brief 通过中国乘联会数据指出，2026年9月新能源车占新车销量67%，在油价上升和燃油车需求下滑的背景下，电动化已从政策扶持转向市场自我强化，并开始通过出口扩张影响全球汽车产业与石油需求。
items.core_argument_en: Using China Passenger Car Association data, Carbon Brief shows that new-energy vehicles reached 67% of new car sales in September 2026, indicating that electrification is shifting from subsidy-led expansion toward self-reinforcing market growth and now affects global auto trade and oil demand through exports and transport substitution.
items.why_now_zh: 这一变化发生在霍尔木兹危机推高燃油成本之后，说明外部能源冲击正在加速交通电动化，而不是只造成短期扰动。2026年9月的销量数据也为观察中国汽车市场结构转折提供了最新窗口。
items.why_now_en: The shift comes after the Hormuz crisis raised fuel costs, suggesting that external energy shocks are accelerating transport electrification rather than merely causing temporary disruption. The September 2026 sales data provide the latest window into a structural turn in China’s auto market.
items.agenda_position_zh: 处于中国交通电动化、石油需求变化与汽车出口竞争三重议程的交汇点。
items.agenda_position_en: This sits at the intersection of China’s transport electrification agenda, changing oil demand, and export competition in the auto industry.

items.title_en: Experts: How are climate scientists using artificial intelligence?
items.summary_zh: Carbon Brief 汇集多位专家意见指出，AI 已进入天气预测、卫星图像分析和气候政策支持等环节，但其算力消耗、结果可验证性不足及对科研不平等的放大效应，意味着科研机构需要同时建立验证标准、能耗约束和公平使用框架。

terms.explanation_zh: 国家、国际组织和非国家行为体围绕共同问题形成规则、协调行动和分配责任的机制。

items.core_argument_zh: Carbon Brief 汇集多位专家意见指出，AI 已进入天气预测、卫星图像分析和气候政策支持等环节，但其算力消耗、结果可验证性不足及对科研不平等的放大效应，意味着科研机构需要同时建立验证标准、能耗约束和公平使用框架。
items.core_argument_en: By assembling expert views, Carbon Brief shows that AI is now being used in weather prediction, satellite-image analysis and climate-policy support, but its energy demand, weak verifiability and tendency to widen scientific inequalities imply that research institutions need validation standards, energy constraints and equitable access rules at the same time.
items.why_now_zh: AI 热潮正在迅速进入气候科学工作流，若缺乏方法审查与资源分配规则，工具效能可能伴随新的偏差和不平等。本文及时回应了这一扩张窗口中的治理缺口。
items.why_now_en: The AI boom is rapidly entering climate-science workflows; without method checks and allocation rules, gains in performance may come with new bias and inequality. The piece responds to this governance gap at the moment of expansion.

items.title_en: Climate may have slipped down the Annual Meetings agenda, but remains on the balance sheet
items.summary_zh: E3G 认为，曼谷 IMF-世界银行年会表面上弱化了气候议题，但能源安全、极端天气与财政约束仍把气候风险留在国家资产负债表上，因此多边开发银行和融资工具必须把预防性适应投资与灾后快速支持纳入常规金融安排。

terms.explanation_zh: 国家、国际组织和非国家行为体围绕共同问题形成规则、协调行动和分配责任的机制。

items.core_argument_zh: E3G 认为，曼谷 IMF-世界银行年会表面上弱化了气候议题，但能源安全、极端天气与财政约束仍把气候风险留在国家资产负债表上，因此多边开发银行和融资工具必须把预防性适应投资与灾后快速支持纳入常规金融安排。
items.core_argument_en: E3G argues that climate may have receded from the main stage at the Bangkok IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, but energy insecurity, extreme weather and fiscal pressure still keep climate risk on governments’ balance sheets, so multilateral development banks and finance tools must embed preventive adaptation investment and rapid post-shock support in routine financial arrangements.
items.why_now_zh: 这篇文章抓住年会窗口，说明气候不再只是议程文本中的高调话题，而是被财政和风险管理逻辑重新编码。它直接回应当前主权融资与适应投资的现实约束。
items.why_now_en: The piece uses the Annual Meetings window to show climate being recoded by fiscal and risk-management logic rather than just by agenda rhetoric. It responds directly to current constraints on sovereign finance and adaptation investment.
items.agenda_position_zh: 处于IMF-世界银行年会、开发融资与气候风险主流化的交叉节点。
items.agenda_position_en: This sits at the intersection of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, development finance and the mainstreaming of climate risk.

items.title_en: EU ETS – Foundation for a Green Steel Ecosystem
items.summary_zh: E3G 认为，欧盟碳排放交易体系（EU ETS）只有与配套立法、需求侧信号和产业政策联动，才能把先锋企业的绿色钢铁计划转化为可融资、可复制的低碳产能，否则转型会停留在个别项目而难形成体系。

items.core_argument_en: E3G argues that the EU Emissions Trading System can support green steel only if it is paired with complementary legislation, demand-side signals and industrial policy; otherwise pioneering projects will not become financeable, replicable low-carbon capacity and the transition will remain fragmented.
items.why_now_zh: 欧洲正在把重工业减排从示范项目推进到体系构建阶段，这使得碳价、法规和市场培育的组合是否到位成为当下关键。文章把ETS从单一减排工具提升为产业生态的制度底座。

readings.title: Multilateral Climate Finance in Pursuit of Private Capital: How the De-Risking Agenda Is Changing International Organizations
readings.note_zh: 本文指出，多边气候融资正在被“去风险化（de-risking）”议程重塑：国际组织越来越把多边资金用来撬动机构投资者和国内银行，而不是直接投向单个减缓或适应项目，这模糊了经济类与环境类国际组织的边界，也带来透明度问题。
readings.note_en: The article argues that multilateral climate finance is being reshaped by a de-risking agenda: international organizations increasingly use multilateral funds to mobilize institutional investors and domestic banks rather than finance individual mitigation or adaptation projects, blurring the line between economic and environmental IOs and creating transparency problems.
readings.methodology_zh: 作者通过对五个气候融资体制内国际组织的增资文件进行文本分析，并结合全球环境基金（GEF）与绿色气候基金（GCF）项目评估，比较去风险化如何改变资金用途与组织角色。
readings.method_en: The authors combine text analysis of replenishment documents from five climate-finance international organizations with an assessment of GEF and GCF projects to compare how de-risking changes funding use and organizational roles.
readings.today_connection_zh: 可与 E3G 的《Climate may have slipped down the Annual Meetings agenda, but remains on the balance sheet》并读，理解为何适应与风险融资正在被重写进多边金融规则。
readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside E3G’s "Climate may have slipped down the Annual Meetings agenda, but remains on the balance sheet" to see how adaptation and risk finance are being rewritten into multilateral financial rules.

research_directions.question_en: Who benefits from de-risking in multilateral climate finance?
How does de-risking reshape climate-finance allocation?

readings.abstract_en: Abstract In the last decade, international financial institutions have advocated that multilateral funding be leveraged to reduce the risk of institutional investors, such as pensions and mutual funds, mobilizing private capital for development and decarbonization. Have international organizations (IOs) that deliver climate finance adopted the de-risking agenda? How is it affecting their work? Through a text analysis of the replenishment documents of five IOs in the climate finance regime, and an assessment of Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Green Climate Fund (GCF) projects, we find that de-risking is reshaping IO activities in three ways. First, the central idea that multilateral climate funding should be used to mobilize institutional investors is widespread across IOs in the climate finance regime. Second, in funding this work, GCF and GEF act as financial advisers to states and domestic banks, erasing the traditional boundary between economic and environmental IOs. Third, when de-risking, IOs often commit multilateral funding to financial institutions to facilitate their lending, rather than to individual mitigation or adaptation projects. This represents a fundamental shift in how multilateral climate funding is spent and raises transparency issues that make it difficult to assess the efficacy of de-risking efforts.

readings.title: Theorizing Access in Global Environmental Governance: A Critical Analysis of COP26 and the COVID-19 Pandemic
readings.authors: Lauren M. Baker, Diana K. Elhard, Kimberly R. Marion Suiseeya, Laura Zanotti, Margaret O’Connell, Alexandra Anderson
readings.note_zh: 本文主张，全球环境治理中的“准入”不能只理解为参会名额或开放注册；COP26 的协作事件民族志显示，歧视性设计、技术差异与认知不公会阻碍持续、有效的参与，并放大权力差距。
readings.note_en: The article argues that access in global environmental governance cannot be reduced to attendance or open registration; collaborative event ethnography at COP26 shows that discriminatory design, technological disparities and recognitional injustice obstruct sustained, meaningful participation and deepen power asymmetries.
readings.methodology_zh: 作者采用COP26的协作事件民族志（collaborative event ethnography），并引入批判性残障研究（critical disability studies）来重构准入、可达性与包容性的差异。
readings.method_en: The authors use collaborative event ethnography at COP26 and draw on critical disability studies to rethink the differences among access, accessibility and inclusion.
readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期关于 COP17 生物多样性谈判程序与《Battleground Ballots》一起看，理解会议可达性与政治动员如何共同塑造治理结果。
readings.today_connection_en: Read with this issue’s COP17 biodiversity process stories and Inside Climate News’s "Battleground Ballots" to see how accessibility and political mobilization jointly shape governance outcomes.

research_directions.question_zh: 会议可达性如何影响结果？
research_directions.question_en: How does conference accessibility affect negotiation outcomes?

research_directions.question_zh: 技术门槛放大了什么不平等？
research_directions.question_en: How do technological barriers amplify inequality in climate diplomacy?

readings.abstract_en: Abstract Sites of global environmental governance (GEG), like the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change Conference of Parties (UNFCCC COP), are critical spaces where state and nonstate actors grapple with our planet’s most pressing challenges. Failure to address the unequal impacts of the climate crisis has led scholars and decision makers to call for more transparent, inclusive, and accountable decision-making processes. However, the ever-increasing number and variety of participants has failed to translate into more equitable outcomes. How do institutional structures and relations of power at sites of GEG privilege certain actors and shape participant experiences? This article argues for a retheorization of access in GEG. Based on collaborative event ethnography at COP26, we find that discriminatory design, technological disparities, and recognitional injustice hamper meaningful sustained access, reify power disparities, and undermine inclusion. Integrating critical disability studies, we show how the COVID-19 pandemic drew into sharper focus the distinctions among inclusion, access, and accessibility that structure GEG and can offer lessons for addressing these inequities.

overview_en: This week’s signal is that electrification, AI and industrial decarbonization are all moving into institutional design.
weekly_thread_zh: 共同问题不是技术是否存在，而是这些技术如何被制度化：电动车扩散、AI进入气候科学、绿色钢铁依赖政策与市场架构。
weekly_thread_en: The shared question is not whether the technologies exist, but how they are institutionalized: EV diffusion, AI in climate science, and green steel all depend on policy and market architecture.

terms.explanation_zh: 国家、国际组织和非国家行为体围绕共同问题形成规则、协调行动和分配责任的机制。

research_signals.core_argument_zh: E3G 认为，曼谷 IMF-世界银行年会表面上弱化了气候议题，但能源安全、极端天气与财政约束仍把气候风险留在国家资产负债表上，因此多边开发银行和融资工具必须把预防性适应投资与灾后快速支持纳入常规金融安排。
research_signals.core_argument_en: E3G argues that climate may have receded from the main stage at the Bangkok IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, but energy insecurity, extreme weather and fiscal pressure still keep climate risk on governments’ balance sheets, so multilateral development banks and finance tools must embed preventive adaptation investment and rapid post-shock support in routine financial arrangements.
research_signals.why_now_zh: 这篇文章抓住年会窗口，说明气候不再只是议程文本中的高调话题，而是被财政和风险管理逻辑重新编码。它直接回应当前主权融资与适应投资的现实约束。
research_signals.why_now_en: The piece uses the Annual Meetings window to show climate being recoded by fiscal and risk-management logic rather than just by agenda rhetoric. It responds directly to current constraints on sovereign finance and adaptation investment.
research_signals.agenda_position_zh: 处于IMF-世界银行年会、开发融资与气候风险主流化的交叉节点。
research_signals.agenda_position_en: This sits at the intersection of the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings, development finance and the mainstreaming of climate risk.
research_signals.why_it_matters_zh: 这篇文章抓住年会窗口，说明气候不再只是议程文本中的高调话题，而是被财政和风险管理逻辑重新编码。它直接回应当前主权融资与适应投资的现实约束。
research_signals.why_it_matters_en: The piece uses the Annual Meetings window to show climate being recoded by fiscal and risk-management logic rather than just by agenda rhetoric. It responds directly to current constraints on sovereign finance and adaptation investment.

research_signals.title_en: EU ETS – Foundation for a Green Steel Ecosystem
research_signals.summary_zh: E3G 认为，欧盟碳排放交易体系（EU ETS）只有与配套立法、需求侧信号和产业政策联动，才能把先锋企业的绿色钢铁计划转化为可融资、可复制的低碳产能，否则转型会停留在个别项目而难形成体系。

terms.explanation_zh: 国家、国际组织和非国家行为体围绕共同问题形成规则、协调行动和分配责任的机制。

research_signals.core_argument_zh: E3G 认为，欧盟碳排放交易体系（EU ETS）只有与配套立法、需求侧信号和产业政策联动，才能把先锋企业的绿色钢铁计划转化为可融资、可复制的低碳产能，否则转型会停留在个别项目而难形成体系。
research_signals.core_argument_en: E3G argues that the EU Emissions Trading System can support green steel only if it is paired with complementary legislation, demand-side signals and industrial policy; otherwise pioneering projects will not become financeable, replicable low-carbon capacity and the transition will remain fragmented.
research_signals.why_now_zh: 欧洲正在把重工业减排从示范项目推进到体系构建阶段，这使得碳价、法规和市场培育的组合是否到位成为当下关键。文章把ETS从单一减排工具提升为产业生态的制度底座。
research_signals.why_now_en: Europe is moving heavy-industry decarbonization from pilots to system-building, making the adequacy of the carbon-price, regulatory and market-building mix a live issue. The piece recasts the ETS as institutional foundation rather than a stand-alone abatement tool.
research_signals.agenda_position_zh: 处于欧盟工业脱碳、碳市场设计与竞争力政策的交汇议程。
research_signals.agenda_position_en: This sits at the intersection of EU industrial decarbonization, carbon-market design and competitiveness policy.
research_signals.why_it_matters_zh: 欧洲正在把重工业减排从示范项目推进到体系构建阶段，这使得碳价、法规和市场培育的组合是否到位成为当下关键。文章把ETS从单一减排工具提升为产业生态的制度底座。
research_signals.why_it_matters_en: Europe is moving heavy-industry decarbonization from pilots to system-building, making the adequacy of the carbon-price, regulatory and market-building mix a live issue. The piece recasts the ETS as institutional foundation rather than a stand-alone abatement tool.

classic_readings.title: Multilateral Climate Finance in Pursuit of Private Capital: How the De-Risking Agenda Is Changing International Organizations
classic_readings.note_zh: 本文指出，多边气候融资正在被“去风险化（de-risking）”议程重塑：国际组织越来越把多边资金用来撬动机构投资者和国内银行，而不是直接投向单个减缓或适应项目，这模糊了经济类与环境类国际组织的边界，也带来透明度问题。
classic_readings.note_en: The article argues that multilateral climate finance is being reshaped by a de-risking agenda: international organizations increasingly use multilateral funds to mobilize institutional investors and domestic banks rather than finance individual mitigation or adaptation projects, blurring the line between economic and environmental IOs and creating transparency problems.
classic_readings.methodology_zh: 作者通过对五个气候融资体制内国际组织的增资文件进行文本分析，并结合全球环境基金（GEF）与绿色气候基金（GCF）项目评估，比较去风险化如何改变资金用途与组织角色。
classic_readings.method_en: The authors combine text analysis of replenishment documents from five climate-finance international organizations with an assessment of GEF and GCF projects to compare how de-risking changes funding use and organizational roles.
classic_readings.today_connection_zh: 可与 E3G 的《Climate may have slipped down the Annual Meetings agenda, but remains on the balance sheet》并读，理解为何适应与风险融资正在被重写进多边金融规则。
classic_readings.today_connection_en: Read alongside E3G’s "Climate may have slipped down the Annual Meetings agenda, but remains on the balance sheet" to see how adaptation and risk finance are being rewritten into multilateral financial rules.

research_directions.question_en: Who benefits from de-risking in multilateral climate finance?
How does de-risking reshape climate-finance allocation?

classic_readings.abstract_en: Abstract In the last decade, international financial institutions have advocated that multilateral funding be leveraged to reduce the risk of institutional investors, such as pensions and mutual funds, mobilizing private capital for development and decarbonization. Have international organizations (IOs) that deliver climate finance adopted the de-risking agenda? How is it affecting their work? Through a text analysis of the replenishment documents of five IOs in the climate finance regime, and an assessment of Global Environment Facility (GEF) and Green Climate Fund (GCF) projects, we find that de-risking is reshaping IO activities in three ways. First, the central idea that multilateral climate funding should be used to mobilize institutional investors is widespread across IOs in the climate finance regime. Second, in funding this work, GCF and GEF act as financial advisers to states and domestic banks, erasing the traditional boundary between economic and environmental IOs. Third, when de-risking, IOs often commit multilateral funding to financial institutions to facilitate their lending, rather than to individual mitigation or adaptation projects. This represents a fundamental shift in how multilateral climate funding is spent and raises transparency issues that make it difficult to assess the efficacy of de-risking efforts.

classic_readings.title: Theorizing Access in Global Environmental Governance: A Critical Analysis of COP26 and the COVID-19 Pandemic
classic_readings.authors: Lauren M. Baker, Diana K. Elhard, Kimberly R. Marion Suiseeya, Laura Zanotti, Margaret O’Connell, Alexandra Anderson
classic_readings.note_zh: 本文主张，全球环境治理中的“准入”不能只理解为参会名额或开放注册；COP26 的协作事件民族志显示，歧视性设计、技术差异与认知不公会阻碍持续、有效的参与，并放大权力差距。
classic_readings.note_en: The article argues that access in global environmental governance cannot be reduced to attendance or open registration; collaborative event ethnography at COP26 shows that discriminatory design, technological disparities and recognitional injustice obstruct sustained, meaningful participation and deepen power asymmetries.
classic_readings.methodology_zh: 作者采用COP26的协作事件民族志（collaborative event ethnography），并引入批判性残障研究（critical disability studies）来重构准入、可达性与包容性的差异。
classic_readings.method_en: The authors use collaborative event ethnography at COP26 and draw on critical disability studies to rethink the differences among access, accessibility and inclusion.
classic_readings.today_connection_zh: 可与本期关于 COP17 生物多样性谈判程序与《Battleground Ballots》一起看，理解会议可达性与政治动员如何共同塑造治理结果。
classic_readings.today_connection_en: Read with this issue’s COP17 biodiversity process stories and Inside Climate News’s "Battleground Ballots" to see how accessibility and political mobilization jointly shape governance outcomes.

research_directions.question_zh: 会议可达性如何影响结果？
research_directions.question_en: How does conference accessibility affect negotiation outcomes?

research_directions.question_zh: 技术门槛放大了什么不平等？
research_directions.question_en: How do technological barriers amplify inequality in climate diplomacy?

classic_readings.abstract_en: Abstract Sites of global environmental governance (GEG), like the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change Conference of Parties (UNFCCC COP), are critical spaces where state and nonstate actors grapple with our planet’s most pressing challenges. Failure to address the unequal impacts of the climate crisis has led scholars and decision makers to call for more transparent, inclusive, and accountable decision-making processes. However, the ever-increasing number and variety of participants has failed to translate into more equitable outcomes. How do institutional structures and relations of power at sites of GEG privilege certain actors and shape participant experiences? This article argues for a retheorization of access in GEG. Based on collaborative event ethnography at COP26, we find that discriminatory design, technological disparities, and recognitional injustice hamper meaningful sustained access, reify power disparities, and undermine inclusion. Integrating critical disability studies, we show how the COVID-19 pandemic drew into sharper focus the distinctions among inclusion, access, and accessibility that structure GEG and can offer lessons for addressing these inequities.

issue_title_en: Electric vehicles, climate AI and green steel in transition
issue_title_zh: 电动车、气候AI与绿色钢铁的转型

title_support.angle_en: This supports the 'electric vehicles' strand by showing China’s EV share reaching a record 67% of new car sales, with electrification accelerating under price and supply shifts.
This supports the 'climate AI' strand by examining how AI is being used across forecasting, satellite analysis and policy support, while flagging risks that shape how the tool is governed.
This supports the 'green steel' strand by arguing that the EU ETS can underpin a broader industrial ecosystem only if legislation and market design align around low-carbon production.
